prerequisites: Knowledge of engineering mathematics or mathematics for computer science.
Procedural and object-oriented programming in C/C++.

learning_outcomes.text: Students will gain fundamental knowledge about control engineering safety systems, reliability considerations, and software quality criteria and their special development requirements. In particular, they will know the processes of functionally safe software development for these systems.

Students will possess the knowledge of how software for safe systems is structured. They will know the design process and tools for creating hardware and software for safe and reliable computer systems. They will understand the concepts of software quality assurance.
Students who have successfully completed this module will understand the fundamentals of Functional Safety and its requirements for development and quality standards.

Students will be able to apply the knowledge acquired in the module and interpret the applicability of functional safety standards to real problems. They will be able to independently make scientifically sound judgments and evaluations for practical scenarios.

Students will be able to communicate comprehensively, plan, and effectively collaborate with other team members to create a multidisciplinary project related to various areas of functional safety, such as hardware, software, and verification and validation.

syllabus_topics: Definition of the terms "hazards and risks", safety vs security.
Fundamentals of reliability considerations (redundancies, diversity, failure rates).
Fundamental importance of metrics and characteristic values of Functional Safety (SIL, ASIL, PL, DC, HFT, MTTF, etc).
SW Quality Management for error prevention in the development process, e.g., V-model.
The use and qualification of development tools for the development of safe software systems.
Coding guidelines and qualification of programming languages.
Basic techniques for error prevention in system architectures.
assessment_rules: The graded examination performance consists of either a written exam or a project report. The choice of the examination type is at the discretion of the lecturer. The project report should be approximately 10-15 pages long with an associated explanation of about 20 minutes. The ungraded examination performance is experimental work, consisting of approximately 8 experiments in total.
